proof_summary: For an arbitrary proposed bound, apply the hypothesis at \(n=(N+6)!/6\); bounding either the Sophie Germain prime or the twin pair makes the relevant prime divide the factorial and hence the complementary prime summand, forcing the two summands to coincide (apart from the impossible divisor \(1\) case). That coincidence gives \(12x-1=3(4y+1)\), contradicting the required primality, so neither family can be bounded.
